title: Perfect-closure criterion for geometric normality
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A$ be a commutative $k$-algebra, and let $P/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Write $q=1$ in characteristic zero and $q=p$ in characteristic $p>0$. Assume that every $x\in P$ satisfies $x^{q^n}\in k$ for some $n\ge0$, and that $P$ is perfect (the Frobenius is surjective in positive characteristic). Then the following are equivalent: (1) the tensor-product algebra $P\otimes_k A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], meaning that each prime localization is an integrally closed domain; (2) for every field extension $E/k$, $E\otimes_k A$ is a normal ring. No finite-type, Noetherian or nonzero hypothesis is imposed on $A$.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, equivalence (4) and (1); Tag 046W, label lemma-perfection, uniqueness identifies P as the perfect closure.

proof.text: For the reverse implication specialize the universal condition to a universe lift of P and transport prime localizations along the tensor equivalence induced by ULift.algEquiv. For the forward implication only perfection of P is needed: every purely inseparable extension of k embeds into P; the power condition on P is therefore not needed in that direction.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, first paragraph and identification of the perfect closure

proof.text: Let k₁/k be a finite purely inseparable extension. Mathlib IsPurelyInseparable.instNonemptyAlgHomOfPerfectField supplies a k-algebra embedding f : k₁ → P, uniquely determined since purely inseparable embeddings into a field are unique. Equip P with the k₁-algebra structure induced by f. Tensor commutativity and cancelBaseChange identify (k₁ ⊗[k] A) ⊗[k₁] P with P ⊗[k] A. Transport normal prime localizations along this equivalence and apply normal_ring_of_normal_tensor_field to obtain normality of k₁ ⊗[k] A.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, paragraph proving (4) implies (3)

proof.text: Fix a finitely generated field extension $K/k$. Apply the make-separable lemma to obtain a commuting square $k\to k_1\to K_1$ and $k\to K\to K_1$, with $k_1/k$ and $K_1/K$ finite purely inseparable and $K_1/k_1$ separable. The extension $K_1/k_1$ is finitely generated: generators of $K/k$ together with a finite $K$-vector-space basis of $K_1$ generate $K_1$ as a field over $k$, and hence over $k_1$. Thus the smooth-fraction-field lemma gives a smooth $k_1$-subalgebra $B\subset K_1$ whose fraction field is $K_1$. Step 2 gives normality of $C=k_1\otimes_k A$.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, paragraph proving (3) implies (2), diagram and smooth algebra

proof.text: By smooth base change the map $C\to R=C\otimes_{k_1}B$ is smooth. Since $C$ is normal, smooth ascent makes $R$ normal. These results allow arbitrary commutative $C$; we make no domain or Noetherian assumption on $A$ or $C$.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, paragraph proving (3) implies (2), Steps 1 and 2

proof.text: Let $S=B\setminus\{0\}$. Since $K_1=S^{-1}B$, localization base change identifies $C\otimes_{k_1}K_1$ with the localization $T$ of $R=C\otimes_{k_1}B$ at the images of $S$. For each prime $\mathfrak q$ of $T$, let $\mathfrak r$ be its inverse image in $R$. Every inverted element is outside $\mathfrak r$. The maps between $T_{\mathfrak q}$ and $R_{\mathfrak r}$ send a fraction $(a/s)/(b/t)$ to $at/(sb)$ and send $a/b$ to $(a/1)/(b/1)$; the denominator $b$ lies outside $\mathfrak r$, and the maps are well-defined inverse ring maps by cross multiplication. Since $R$ is normal, $R_{\mathfrak r}$ is an integrally closed domain. Thus every $T_{\mathfrak q}$ is an integrally closed domain and $T$ is normal. The tensor maps $C\otimes_{k_1}K_1\to K_1\otimes_k A$, $(x\otimes a)\otimes z\mapsto zx\otimes a$, and $z\otimes a\mapsto(1\otimes a)\otimes z$ are inverse by balancing and the tensor universal property. Hence $K_1\otimes_k A$ is normal.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, paragraph proving (3) implies (2), Step 3; localization argument omitted in lemma-localization-normal-ring

proof.text: The inverse tensor maps $(x\otimes a)\otimes z\mapsto zx\otimes a$ and $z\otimes a\mapsto(1\otimes a)\otimes z$ identify $(K\otimes_k A)\otimes_K K_1$ with $K_1\otimes_k A$. Apply normality descent along the field extension $K_1/K$. Therefore $K\otimes_k A$ is normal for every finitely generated $K/k$.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, paragraph proving (3) implies (2), Step 4

proof.text: For any extension E/k, index by finite subsets s of E, ordered by inclusion, and put K_s = k(s). The tensor rings K_s ⊗[k] A and inclusion maps form a filtered diagram. Every element of E ⊗[k] A comes from a stage: use tensor induction, put a pure tensor x ⊗ a in the singleton stage {x}, and put a sum in the union of the two finite stages. Each canonical map K_s ⊗[k] A → E ⊗[k] A is injective because A is a flat k-vector space. Hence equality of two elements at a fixed stage already holds there. The filtered-colimit criterion for underlying types and reflection by the ring forgetful functor establish that E ⊗[k] A is the colimit of the diagram.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, paragraph proving (2) implies (1), directed tensor-colimit identification

proof.text: Every stage of this directed diagram is normal by Step 6. The filtered-colimit normality lemma makes its colimit $E\otimes_k A$ normal. Since $E/k$ was arbitrary this proves (2). If $A=0$, all tensor algebras are zero rings and normality is vacuous because there are no prime ideals.

source.place: Tag 037Z, label lemma-geometrically-normal, paragraph proving (2) implies (1), conclusion
